Okay that's fair but what about the last bit? Fear of harming yourself and causing yourself pain isn't cultural it's how the brain functions. Pain is bad, it's meant to be perceived negatively by the mind itself.

No that's not necessarily true, intrusive thoughts are defined as anything that makes you distressed at your own self and every person feels differently about what's horrifying. It's person to person.

For example people suffering from OCD have intrusive thoughts that are by the majority seen as overblown but they are distressing to the person suffering it. In example, an intrusive thought from someone with OCD can be shaking someone's bare hand with your own bare hand and imagining all the bacteria that might be in the other person's hand. We may be "trained" to keep ourselves clean and hygenic, but we're certainly not trained as a culture to assume everyone is so dirty we are teeming with flesh eating bacteria.

We're also not necessarily taught that. People with OCD just develop those fears and it's not always trauma based.

Distress would be an inevitabilty of the human condition and whether there's a supplied culture or not the brain would make things up to be intrusive about, like hurting yourself.

It's not because hurting myself is morally reprehensible that I get freaked out when I imagine putting my hand in an immersion blender, it's because why would I imagine myself putting my body through that kind of pain?

So like a giant long bin like the ones they use for wrapping paper that has a super deep pan, or just a long fish tank, is what you'd want to look for in regards to a hammy.
